newsitem.title: UK: Daimler H1 profit doubles on cars, currencies.
newsitem.headline: Daimler H1 profit doubles on cars, currencies.

text.p: German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG said on Thursday its group operating profit more than doubled in the first half of 1997 to 1.849 billion marks from 827 million marks in the same period a year earlier.

The group, Germany's largest, said surging car sales, the weak mark and strict internal cost control were behind the improved performance. It also predicted that its full-year performance would be significantly better than 1996.

"The programmes to increase efficiency have continued to improve operating results," said chief executive officer Juergen Schrempp. "Though we are not yet satisfied with the overall level of profitability, we are beginning to achieve the sort of returns we want."

Daimler's sales of its Mercedes-Benz cars rose six percent to 335,794 and Daimler said it hoped to build and sell over 700,000 in the full year. Sales of commercial vehicles rose 14 percent to 191,994.

The automotive division made an operating profit of 1.429 billion marks, up only slightly from 1.409 billion in the first half of 1996 due to high costs related to the launch of new models such as the small A-Class car.
All the profit came from the car division with commercial vehicles making a small, unspecified loss. But Schrempp said he expected the commercial vehicles to make a profit this year.
Analysts said the half-year report was on the weak side of expectations but that they remained confident in Daimler's financial performance.

"They are just below our estimates. I was looking for about 2.05 billion marks in operating profit. But I am relatively encouraged by the comments for the second half of the year, " said Andrew Blair-Smith, analyst at BZW in Frankfurt.
"I think Daimler will report a significantly better operating profit for the second half," he said, forecasting 4.7 billion marks compared with the 1996 level of 2.4 billion marks.

Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), for years a huge drag on group earnings, finally swung back into the black, turning in an operating profit of 74 million marks, compared to a loss of 677 million marks in the first six months of 1996.

It particularly benefited from the strong dollar in which its aircraft sales are denominated. Huge losses at Dasa related to its disposal of Dutch aircraft maker Fokker forced the group to a seven billion mark loss in 1995. Debis and Daimler's rail and electronics businesses were also in profit.

Although the weak mark, which has fallen around 20 percent against the dollar this year, boosted the company's earnings, profits would have been even higher were it not for Daimler's hedging programme.
Chief Financial Officer Manfred Gentz said, "Operating profit would have been 400 to 500 million marks higher if we hadn't hedged for currencies."

Although not yet satisfied with Daimler's profits, Schrempp stressed its earnings power had improved and expected good progress toward meeting an internal goal of seeing 12 percent of return on capital employed.

"If we assume second half proift would be the same as the first half, then our full-year return on capital employed would be eight to nine percent," he told reporters at the company's half-year results conference.
